messages.author: e3973a682064049e
messages.subject: Model comparison_Chisq diff shows different results
parts:
Hi there,

I am comparing two models.
In one model, the paths are allowed to differ; the other are constrained to be equal.

model1 <- "
    #measurement    
    IV =~ var1 + var2 + var3 + var4 + var5
    
     med1 =~ var6 + ... + varvar11
     med2 =~ var12 + ... + var17

     DV =~ var18 + ... + varvar25
    
     #structural
     med1 + med2 ~ IV
     DV ~ IV + med1 + med2
"

model2 <- "
   #measurement    
    IV =~ var1 + var2 + var3 + var4 + var5
    
     med1 =~ var6 + ... + varvar11
     med2 =~ var12 + ... + var17

     DV =~ var18 + ... + varvar25
    
     #structural
     med1 + med2 ~ IV
     DV ~ IV + a*med1 + a*med2
"
anova(model1_fit, model2_fit, test = "Chisq")

Results:
Model1: RMSEA = .069      CFI = .960       Chisq = 3037.391        df = 269
Model2: RMSEA = .070      CFI = .959       Chisq =  3108.633       df = 270

The difference between chisq is 3108.633 - 3037.391 = 71.242;

BUT the anova results showed that Chisq diff = 62.588.

Does anyone understand why the results are different? Thanks in advance!

Best,
Serena

parts:
Then in the output, you should see something like this:

Scaled Chi-Squared Difference Test (method = “satorra.bentler.2001”)

lavaan NOTE:
    The “Chisq” column contains standard test statistics, not the
    robust test that should be reported per model. A robust difference
    test is a function of two standard (not robust) statistics.

With MLR, the chi-square difference test is computed differently, unlike the usual chi-square difference test. You can check the corresponding referenece from the printout, Satorra and Bentler 2001 in the above example, though the method used may be different in your case.

Hope this helps.

-- Shu Fai

parts: > So I need to report the scaled chi square for each model separately. But rely on anova results to report the Chisq diff, and p-value, right?
Usually, yes. But your model has clusters and I am not sure whether there are any special concerns in this case. Maybe other members can help.

> b. I tried to remove the argument estimator = "MLR" or change it to "ML". The results are the same as the MLR results.
> If with MLR, the chi-square difference test is computed differently, then not using MLR will be different with it. But I got the same results. I am confused with this, could you please help me with this?

https://rdrr.io/cran/lavaan/man/lavTest.html

The argument estimator = "MLR" just represts a collection of settings, one of them the test statistic. May you share the call to sem/cfa?

-- Shu Fai

I am not sure there is argument "test" for anova():

https://rdrr.io/cran/lavaan/man/lavTestLRT.html

Usually, lavTestLRT() (and anova() for lavaan objects) should be able to select the appropriate method bsaed on the test statistic requested. Perhaps you can just call lavTestLRT() or anova() and let it do the job, without setting any additional arguments unless you are sure you need to.

--- Shu Fai

parts: I am not sure there is argument "test" for anova():

lavaan will detect which (robust) test was requested, and conduct the appropriate difference test.  But if you requested a vector of multiple lavaan(test=) values, then lavaan picks the first robust one by default.  You can use the new (0.6-18) lavTestLRT(test=) argument to specify a different one, if that is ever relevant (usually not).
